To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the socialization process in an open source software community is a complex, multi-faceted, and dynamic process, that involves both individual and collective learning, and is shaped by the social and technical aspects of software development.
the socialization of newcomers into OSS projects is a complex process that involves a combination of learning and political activities.

socialization in the OSS community studied is characterized by a process of progressive integration into the community, which is punctuated by the acquisition of a new identity and the development of a new network of allies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and political aspects of software development, and the role of software in the reproduction and transformation of the communities that develop it.
understanding how socialization in OSS communities is accomplished, and how it can be supported.
the social and technical processes through which new members of OSS communities are progressively integrated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
socialization in OSS communities can be seen as an individual learning and identity construction process, as well as a political process of alliance building.

socialization in OSS development communities is a complex process that involves both the progressive construction of a personal identity as software craftsmen and the progressive construction of political alliances to support the individual’s efforts.
OSS communities have been able to successfully reproduce themselves by integrating newcomers, but only by adopting a very specific model of community organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the socialization process of OSS developers is not a linear one.
socialization is a political process in which newcomers progressively learn how to become part of a community of developers, how to contribute to a project, and how to make their contributions count.
we have been able to identify and describe a process of socialization in OSS communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social and the material are inextricably intertwined in the process of socialization.
the social and material dimensions of OSS development are intertwined, and should be considered together in order to understand how these projects work.

the design of socialization support tools should be informed by the social practices of the communities that will use them, rather than by the practices of other communities or by a priori assumptions of what constitutes good socialization.
